/-!
# Conjecture 10.38

by G. A. Noskov

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«10.38»

/--
Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$, for every $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections? Equivalently, for each such
$n$, is there a bound $N$ such that every element of this elementary subgroup
is a product of at most $N$ matrices $1+c e_{ij}$ with $i \ne j$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.38» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ N : ℕ,
      ∀ A : Matrix (Fin (n + 3)) (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ),
        (∃ L : List (Matrix.TransvectionStruct (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)),
          (L.map Matrix.TransvectionStruct.toMatrix).prod = A) →
        ∃ L : List (Matrix.TransvectionStruct (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)),
          L.length ≤ N ∧ (L.map Matrix.TransvectionStruct.toMatrix).prod = A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.38»
modeling_decisions: Represented ℤ[x₁,…,xₙ] as `MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ` and (n+3)-by-(n+3) matrices using the index type `Fin (n + 3)`.
Represented elementary transvections with Mathlib's `Matrix.TransvectionStruct`; its `hij` field enforces distinct row and column indices, and `toMatrix` is exactly the matrix `1 + c eᵢⱼ`.

Characterized the elementary subgroup directly as matrices admitting a finite transvection factorization. This is the subgroup generated by the transvections because inverses of transvections are transvections.
Placed `∃ N` inside the universal quantifier over `n`, so the breadth bound may depend on the number of variables, as required.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.38

by G. A. Noskov

(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

Here $E_m(R)$ is the elementary subgroup of $SL_m(R)$: the subgroup generated by the
elementary transvections $t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c\,e_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ and $c \in R$.
A group has finite breadth (width) with respect to a generating set $S$ if there is
a bound $N$ such that every element is a product of at most $N$ elements of
$S \cup S^{-1}$. The inverse of the transvection $t_{ij}(c)$ is the transvection
$t_{ij}(-c)$, so here $S^{-1} = S$.

The question is motivated by van der Kallen's theorem that $SL_3(\mathbb{C}[x])$ does
not have bounded word length with respect to the elementary transvections.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- [vdK82] W. van der Kallen, *$SL_3(\mathbb{C}[x])$ does not have bounded word length*,
  Algebraic K-theory, Part I (Oberwolfach, 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 966,
  Springer, 1982, 357–361.
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«10.38»

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The elementary transvection $t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c\,e_{ij}$ ($i \neq j$) as an element of
$SL_n(R)$. -/
def transvectionSL (t : TransvectionStruct n R) : SpecialLinearGroup n R :=
  ⟨t.toMatrix, t.det⟩

variable (n R) in
/-- The elementary subgroup $E_n(R)$ of $SL_n(R)$: the subgroup generated by the elementary
transvections $t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c\,e_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ and $c \in R$. -/
def elementarySubgroup : Subgroup (SpecialLinearGroup n R) :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range transvectionSL)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem transvectionSL_mem_elementarySubgroup (t : TransvectionStruct n R) :
    transvectionSL t ∈ elementarySubgroup n R :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨t, rfl⟩

/--
Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite breadth with respect to
the set of transvections?

That is: for every $n \geq 1$, is there a bound $N$ such that every element of the
elementary subgroup $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$ is a product of at most $N$
elementary transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, $i \neq j$, $c \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$?
The bound $N$ may depend on $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 19 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.38» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ A ∈ elementarySubgroup (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ),
      ∃ L : List (TransvectionStruct (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)),
        L.length ≤ N ∧ (L.map transvectionSL).prod = A := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.38»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (elementary transvections as the generator set, n ≥ 1 as a universal quantifier, N allowed to depend on n) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: 'The set of transvections' is read as the elementary transvections t_{ij}(c) = 1 + c e_{ij}, i ≠ j (the standard generating set of E_m(R)), following the decomposition notes; the alternative reading 'all transvections 1 + u vᵀ with vᵀu = 0' (conjugates included) was not used.

Finite breadth/width is formalized as: ∃ N, every element of E is a product of a list of at most N elementary transvections. Inverses are not listed separately because t_{ij}(c)⁻¹ = t_{ij}(-c) is itself an elementary transvection (verified in Lean in a scratch check), and 'at most N' vs 'exactly N' is harmless since t_{ij}(0) = 1.
E_{n+3}(R) is taken as a subgroup of SL_{n+3}(R) (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin (n+3)) R) rather than GL_{n+3}(R); this is equivalent since all generators have determinant 1.
'n ≥ 1' is an implicit universal quantifier: ∀ n ≥ 1 with n : ℕ (type forced by Fin n / Fin (n+3)); the bound N is allowed to depend on n (∃ N sits inside ∀ n).
ℤ[x_1,…,x_n] is MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ.

One extra @[category API] lemma (transvectionSL_mem_elementarySubgroup, fully proved) is included as a basic API test of the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md; the slot itself is the single theorem kourovka.«10.38».
AMS tags 19 (K-theory) and 20 (group theory) chosen since bounded elementary generation of E_n(R) sits at the interface of algebraic K-theory and group theory.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.38

by G. A. Noskov

(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

Here $E_m(R)$ is the elementary subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$: the subgroup generated by the
(elementary) transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, where $i \neq j$, $c \in R$ and $e_{ij}$ is the
matrix unit with a single $1$ in position $(i, j)$. A group has finite breadth (also called
finite width) with respect to a set of generators $S$ if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that
every element of the group is a product of at most $N$ elements of $S$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Matrix

namespace Kourovka.«10.38»

/-- The set of (elementary) transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, with $i \neq j$ and $c \in R$, viewed
as elements of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$. -/
def elementaryTransvections (m R : Type*) [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R] :
    Set (SpecialLinearGroup m R) :=
  {g | ∃ (i j : m) (c : R), i ≠ j ∧ (g : Matrix m m R) = transvection i j c}

/-- The elementary subgroup $E_m(R)$: the subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_m(R)$ generated by the
transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$, $i \neq j$. -/
def elementarySubgroup (m R : Type*) [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R] :
    Subgroup (SpecialLinearGroup m R) :=
  Subgroup.closure (elementaryTransvections m R)

/-- A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ has finite breadth (width) with respect to a set $S \subseteq G$
if there is a uniform bound $N$ such that every element of $H$ is a product of at most $N$
elements of $S$. -/
def HasFiniteBreadth {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (S : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g ∈ H, ∃ L : List G, (∀ s ∈ L, s ∈ S) ∧ L.length ≤ N ∧ L.prod = g

section API

variable {m R : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing R]

/-- The identity matrix is a transvection (with $c = 0$) as soon as there are two distinct
indices. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma one_mem_elementaryTransvections [Nontrivial m] :
    (1 : SpecialLinearGroup m R) ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij⟩ := exists_pair_ne m
  exact ⟨i, j, 0, hij, by simp⟩

/-- The set of transvections is closed under inverses: $(1 + c\,e_{ij})^{-1} = 1 - c\,e_{ij}$.
Hence breadth with respect to this set does not depend on whether inverses of generators are
allowed. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma inv_mem_elementaryTransvections {g : SpecialLinearGroup m R}
    (hg : g ∈ elementaryTransvections m R) : g⁻¹ ∈ elementaryTransvections m R := by
  obtain ⟨i, j, c, hij, hg⟩ := hg
  refine ⟨i, j, -c, hij, ?_⟩
  have h : g * ⟨transvection i j (-c), det_transvection_of_ne i j hij (-c)⟩ = 1 := by
    ext1
    simp [hg, transvection_mul_transvection_same i j hij]
  rw [inv_eq_of_mul_eq_one_right h]

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma elementaryTransvections_subset_elementarySubgroup :
    elementaryTransvections m R ⊆ elementarySubgroup m R :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure

/-- The trivial subgroup has finite breadth with respect to any set. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
lemma hasFiniteBreadth_bot {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Set G) :
    HasFiniteBreadth (⊥ : Subgroup G) S :=
  ⟨0, fun g hg => ⟨[], by simp, le_rfl, by simpa using hg.symm⟩⟩

end API

/--
(W. van der Kallen). Does $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$, $n \geq 1$, have finite
breadth with respect to the set of transvections?

That is, for every $n \geq 1$, is there a bound $N$ (which may depend on $n$) such that every
element of the elementary subgroup $E_{n+3}(\mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n])$ is a product of at
most $N$ transvections $1 + c\,e_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 19 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.38» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      HasFiniteBreadth (elementarySubgroup (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ))
        (elementaryTransvections (Fin (n + 3)) (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.38»

modeling_decisions: 'Transvections' is interpreted as the elementary transvections 1 + c·e_{ij} (i ≠ j, c ∈ R), following van der Kallen's bounded-word-length setting and the decomposition table, not the more general 'transvections' 1 + u·vᵀ with vᵀu = 0.
E_{n+3}(R) is placed inside Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin (n+3)) R (as Subgroup.closure of the transvections); this is standard since every elementary transvection has determinant 1.

Breadth is measured by products of elements of the set S itself (no explicit inverses). This is equivalent to the usual word length over S ∪ S⁻¹ because the set of elementary transvections is closed under inverses ((1 + c e_{ij})⁻¹ = 1 − c e_{ij}); this is recorded by the API lemma inv_mem_elementaryTransvections. ℤ[x_1,…,x_n] is formalized as MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ; the matrix index type is Fin (n+3), tying matrix size to the number of variables exactly as in the statement.

elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$.

def HasFiniteBreadth {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) (S : Set G) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g ∈ H,
    ∃ L : List G, L.length ≤ N ∧ (∀ x ∈ L, x ∈ S ∪ S⁻¹) ∧ L.prod = g

theorem hasFiniteBreadth_bot {G : Type*} [Group G] (S : Set G) :
    HasFiniteBreadth (⊥ : Subgroup G) S := by
  refine ⟨0, fun g hg => ⟨[], le_rfl, by simp, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hg
  simp [hg]
